body.text: The Knox AAPI Business Association brings its Asian Night Market back to Hi-Wire on Friday for the fall run, six to nine, and it costs nothing to walk in. The association, which exists to promote and give free resources to the area's Asian-owned businesses, curates the lineup; The Thread TN, an Asian and Pacific Islander magazine, presents it. Hi-Wire's whole second floor is the room, so the cold stays outside.
Eat first

Two food trucks park for the night, Happy Song Pocha and Gohan Japanese Grill, and nine food and drink makers set up inside. Ajumom Kimchi brings small-batch kimchi and kimchi-style pickles made in East Tennessee, from spicy napa cabbage to cucumber and daikon, with vegan and gluten-free jars. A Lucky Little Bakery's Ben bakes sogeum ppang, the Korean salt bread, milk bread buns and songpyeon, the harvest-festival rice cake, and they are meant to go home with you. Matcha Mama, Grace Cake, Tealicious and Mama Lana's Kitchen fill out the table.
Then shop

Ten art and retail tables make it the market's own pitch: get ahead on the holidays. Sasa Starcake is new this round with ceramic critter trinkets and little dishes and incense holders; Roshani Designs, Sweet Busy Bee, Swordlinks, Trappd Creations and Nokku Studios sell their goods; Tally Tattoo and Henna by Nia work on the spot. Knox Asian Festival, the UT Vietnamese Student Association and Kimchi Princess hold the nonprofit and student tables. Hi-Wire asks you to carpool or grab a ride, since parking around the building is thin; its neighbor Johnson Architecture is waiving the fee on its lot for the three hours.

body.text: BellTower is the goth night that threw the Halloween house party at The Pink Cactus two weeks ago. Thursday it tries something new: BellTower Presents, a night built around a live band, and the first one is Feyleux, the North Carolina darkwave duo whose new record, Shadeweaver, came out on November 6. The band calls the album an exploration of the shadow self, written over last winter, and describes the sound as darkwave, post-punk and dream pop. The night is billed as live Southern gothic followed by a dark dance party.

Darkness opens on the decks and Cemetery Sex, one of BellTower's regular DJs, closes, spinning goth, darkwave and post-punk in a seventies cocktail lounge, which is Fly by Night's whole idea. Doors are at 8:45, the music at nine, ten dollars, twenty-one and up. Thursday is a rainy one, so the lounge is the right place to be.

body.text: Friday the 13th gets its own holiday on Sevier Avenue. The Pink Cactus, the karaoke-room bar with the big front yard, has been planning Alt Mart since October: a market of what it calls non-mainstream goods and services, art, food, bespoke goods, games, flash tattoos, plants and potions, with the vendors applying through the bar. It is the first one the bar has held, and it is all ages until nine.
The crown

At six the bar crowns one alt baddie MX Knoxville Goth, a pageant hosted by Purrahna Rivers, with live entertainment from Fiona Snap, npotwin420, River Abrasax and DJ Graves around it. The bar's own words for the night: come together to celebrate the differences that make all people unique and special; kindness is key, no hate lives here. The district's November list has it running from four. When the market wraps, the same building turns into a Y2K dance floor at nine, which is its own story below.

body.text: The Forest Speaks is Ijams Nature Center's beginner workshop in nature journaling: an hour and a half on Friday evening learning to look harder at what is in front of you and get it onto paper. The park says no artistic or naturalist experience is necessary and that the point is to become a more intentional observer, with techniques for turning what you notice into words and sketches. The park provides everything, though you can bring a notebook and pens you like. It is fifteen dollars, registration is on the park's event page, and the park's standing assumption-of-risk form has to be on file once a year.

body.text: Block printing is the one where you carve a design into a block, ink it and press it, and then print it as many times as you like, which is the park's whole argument for it. Saturday afternoon Ijams Nature Center runs its beginner class: two hours to draw and carve one four-by-six design, ink it up in several colors and hand-press it onto paper or fabric. The park calls it an easy, sustainable way to breathe new life into old clothes, and invites you to bring anything you want to customize. Eighteen dollars covers the supplies; register on the event page. It is the first of three dates this season, with others on November 29 and December 20.

body.text: Every third Sunday the East Tennessee Bluegrass Association and Ijams Nature Center put chairs in a circle and play, and this month's is Sunday from two to five. It is a community jam, open to any acoustic bluegrass instrument and every skill level: the first hour is the beginner jam, where the tunes are slow and the chord changes get called, and from three to five it opens to everyone. The association draws one line, no harmonicas or spoons at this time. It is free, listeners are welcome, and the park asks for an RSVP. Sunny and 55 means the circle sits outside on the plaza by the visitor center; in bad weather it moves indoors. It is the free afternoon of the weekend.

stories.label: Old Sevier
stories.title: Two more murals are going up along the SoKno Rail Trail & Art Walk: herons and dogwoods at Landing Health, a dulcimer and a marble eagle on the Trimble building
stories.deck: Five paintings and two sculptures along the walk now.

facts.label: What
facts.value: The SoKno Rail Trail & Art Walk · a 3.8-mile rail corridor from Chapman Highway to Ijams Nature Center with a 1.5-mile outdoor gallery

facts.label: New this month
facts.value: Whitney Herrington's herons and oversized dogwood blooms at Landing Health · Key Detail's Appalachian mural, with a mountain dulcimer and a marble eagle, on the Wm S Trimble building

facts.label: Also
facts.value: 37 native trees planted behind Rivers Edge Apartments on Oct 22 · the trail's tunnel is being relit by Massey Electric and CertaPro

facts.label: Who
facts.value: Legacy Parks Foundation · legacyparks.org

body.text: Legacy Parks Foundation says two more murals are being painted right now along the SoKno Rail Trail & Art Walk, the rail corridor it is turning into a soft-surface trail with an outdoor gallery along its middle. Tennessee artist Whitney Herrington's piece at Landing Health is herons and oversized dogwood blooms; at the Wm S Trimble building, New York artist Key Detail is painting Appalachian heritage and Knoxville history together, a mountain dulcimer and a marble eagle among them. They follow Naomi Haverland's fishing lures and Anna Charney's botanicals on the back of Kern's, and two sculptures already stand along the path.

The foundation also planted 37 native trees along the trail behind Rivers Edge Apartments with volunteers on October 22, and this week thanked Massey Electric and CertaPro for the work relighting the tunnel the trail passes through, which it called seeing the light at the end of the tunnel. More installations are promised; the campaign for ten-foot SOKNO letters along the walk is still raising money.
